cost_note: New-paid cost is campaign-wide and shared across lane reports; never add it across lanes. Observed evidence cost retains its original attempt scope. Neither cost is a speed ranking.
hypothesis: One global BISPF public lazy policy at reg_every 4, 8 or 16 preserves every measured eager-control PASS across the unchanged tiered tasks, including held tests, with the base coefficient fixed and the built-in k-fold strength compensation. This measures coupled application-clock controller behavior, not isolated gradient frequency. Any matched PASS-to-FAIL falsifies preservation for that interval; unavailable evidence cannot pass. No seed study, per-task tuning, scientific default adoption or automatic qualification.
interpretation: Public lazy policy including application-clock controllers; internal k-fold strength compensation. Base coefficient, optimizer updates and task protocols remain fixed.

limitations: Fixed-seed measured pass preservation is not statistical noninferiority.
Raw metric deltas have no inferred common scale or improvement direction.
Charged worker wall time is cost, not a speed measurement.
coverage.qualification_note: Comparison readout only; diagnostic coverage grants no ordinary qualification.

recommendation.reason: Finish or repair unavailable matched evidence before selecting a cadence.
